background.text: The story that Lorenzo de' Medici sent Leonardo to Milan with the musician Atalante Migliorotti, bearing a silver lyre for Ludovico, comes from the Anonimo Gaddiano and has no documentary support C . What survives in Leonardo's own hand is the draft letter of self recommendation in the Codex Atlanticus, which lists military engineering first and places painting and sculpture at the end: a first rank source for how Leonardo himself read the structure of demand in the Milanese market A . From about 1490 the documents show him formally installed as a court engineer, with a workshop in the Corte Vecchia, engaged on the clay model of the Sforza horse (exhibited 1493), on festival production (the Festa del Paradiso, 1490), and on advice in canal works and fortification. In June 1490 the fabbrica of Pavia cathedral summoned Leonardo, together with Francesco di Giorgio Martini, to advise on the building; the payment and invitation records survive A . Pavia's patron is Saint Syrus (feast 9 December). His notebooks record the Visconti library in the castle and the antique equestrian statue called the Regisole. At Vigevano, Ludovico's model estate, Leonardo studied the irrigation works and stepped water channels, with a dated entry of 1494 A . Milan held roughly twice the population of Florence, and its market for the arts had a different shape: a single overwhelming purchaser, the court, where Florence dispersed demand among guilds, confraternities, and religious houses. The horizontal spread of Leonardo's employment, from painting to ordnance, hydraulics, and festival machinery, answers that structure of demand. The wealth of a toll state astride the transalpine routes coexisted with exposure to invasion from every quarter, and the collapse of the regime in 1499 ended what would remain the longest residence of Leonardo's life, seventeen years.
